title: P2 browser frozen-base LoRA gradient parity
hypothesis: Burn CPU/WASM and WebGPU can execute the exact frozen-base rank-4 QKV LoRA fixture and export the complete eight-tensor adapter-gradient set within the declared numerical gates without changing the existing dense browser path.

use_case.claim: Qualify broadly accessible browser runtimes for later owner-approved PEFT campaigns before changing the coordinator contract.

baseline.label: Python LoRA oracle
baseline.description: The exact Python FP32 summed-loss gradient fixture with SHA-256 7ce16dfd740fd5a249257de6ab442943577b86917f9ae77604c5097ce1a5b8e2.

primary_metric.label: Adapter-gradient cosine similarity
primary_metric.description: Cosine similarity across all declared adapter-gradient values relative to the Python oracle.

repeated_validation_suite.label: CPU/WASM LoRA parity
repeated_validation_suite.description: Run the exact fixture through Burn Autodiff NdArray in browser WASM and compare every adapter gradient.

final_holdout_suite.label: WebGPU LoRA parity
final_holdout_suite.description: Run the same fixture through Burn Autodiff Wgpu and compare every adapter gradient after CPU semantics are established.

guardrails.label: Complete adapter tensor set
guardrails.description: Exactly 8 tensors and 8,192 values must be exported with the Python names and shapes.

guardrails.label: Summed-loss parity
guardrails.description: Relative summed-loss error must not exceed 0.002.

guardrails.label: Gradient relative L2
guardrails.description: Relative L2 error across the adapter gradients must not exceed 0.01.

guardrails.label: Dense browser regression remains green
guardrails.description: The original 52-tensor CPU/WASM dense fixture must retain its established parity result.

independent_variables.label: Browser execution backend
independent_variables.description: Compare Burn NdArray CPU/WASM with Burn Wgpu WebGPU using the same fixture.

controlled_variables.label: Base, adapter, and batch
controlled_variables.description: Keep the T0 base digest, LoRA manifest, adapter initialization, token batch, summed loss, and Python gradient oracle exact.
